curator_notes: [Mechanistic Bridging -- model-generated hypothesis, not a tested result] Serine/glycine starvation (-SG medium; dietary serine/glycine depletion in vivo) induces a nrf2_ferroptosis signature (protective_resistance) in HCT116; Erastin's reported resistance mechanism runs through the same pathway (GPX4-dependent lipid-peroxide detoxification). resistance_mechanism.mechanism_description: GPX4 detoxifies lipid peroxides downstream of cystine/glutathione depletion; sufficient GPX4 activity (or an intact glutathione pool feeding it) can rescue cells from erastin's system Xc- blockade despite cystine starvation (Dixon et al. 2012; Yang et al. 2014).

protocol_parameters.medium: MEM (21090) + 1x MEM vitamins (11120) + 10% dialysed FBS + 2 mM L-glutamine + 25 mM D-glucose; complete media additionally contains serine 0.4 mM and glycine 0.4 mM; starvation media omit both (-SG)
protocol_parameters.in_vivo_leg: serine/glycine-depleted diet (LC-MS-confirmed drop in serum serine/glycine) in HCT116 xenografts
protocol_parameters.line_context: HCT116 p53+/+ vs isogenic p53-/-; RKO (Supp. Fig. 2); primary MEFs
protocol_parameters.readout: proliferation/viability; LC-MS metabolic flux; p53/p21 immunoblot

modifier.estimated_relative_cost_note: Specialized diet formulation; no equipment, though compliance monitoring (dietary counseling) adds some real-world overhead.

drug.name: Erastin
drug.mechanism_of_action: System Xc- inhibition depletes intracellular cystine, collapsing glutathione synthesis and inducing ferroptosis

mechanism.notes: In p53+/+ HCT116 cells, serine/glycine withdrawal triggers transient p53-p21 (CDKN1A) cell-cycle arrest that promotes survival by channelling depleted serine stores into glutathione synthesis, preserving antioxidant capacity (Nature 2012). Directionality is protective for the p53-WT state under this modifier.
